title: Where a technique is written
verbatim: Signatures own, arts shared. A signature, or any art one person derived alone, gets its own page priced at its owner's exact reserve; a school art lives once on its school's page, priced by Stage band. The card's rows link to either.
question: Where does a character's technique entry live: on its own page, inside the card, or split by kind?

title: Designed first or found in play
verbatim: Core first, rest found. Before first fire the card holds mechanism, cost, limit, tell and counter. Name, forms, Readiness (its casting-time figure), evolutions and What nobody knows fill in from what play showed.
question: How much of a technique must exist on its card before it first fires on the page?

title: Your sketch to a card
verbatim: Whole card, yours to keep. Natalie returns the full R47-2 entry at once, a proposed true name in your character's tongue included; every choice on it (name, call, vow) sticks only when you keep it.
question: When you sketch an ability for your own character, what comes back?

title: Your price against the law
verbatim: Your price, new mechanism. The cost and limit you named stand; Natalie reworks the mechanism until they fall out of it, so R17-4 holds. If no lawful mechanism yields them, she says so in one line and offers the nearest.
question: When your sketch names its own cost and the mechanism derives another, which stands?

title: Techniques on the Crystal
verbatim: Signatures print once. Adds a fifth growth moment to R70-84: the first time a Trait-permitted signature holds, one inline Crystal line names it, its Trait and its Grade. School arts never print.
question: Does the bearer's Crystal ever print a technique?

title: The fairness test
verbatim: Yes to: Same Stage can answer (The written counter is within reach of a prepared practitioner of the technique's own Stage; a counter that needs a higher Stage or a rare Wellspring fails the card); Counter on known law (The counter rests on law someone already knows (a Wellspring's recorded failure, a school's teaching, a Family's weakness), so a player can study toward it before he meets the technique); A counter at each phase (The card names a counter before, during and after contact; 'none once contact is made' fails and the card is rebuilt).
question: Which tests must a technique's Counter pass before its card stands?

title: What opens a new technique
verbatim: Numbers plus a cause. The FOW line must be met, and the technique arrives only with a cause on the page: a teacher named, a book studied, or the problem it answers met in a fight.
question: What lets a character gain a technique he did not have?

title: How long a ladder of forms
verbatim: By the school's culture. Western and Kharven schools run short ladders like Liechtenauer's; the lineage halls and the Korean-stratum houses keep long catalogues. Each school's page sets its count.
question: How many numbered forms does a school's art run?

title: Cutting a chant short
verbatim: Clip it, lose output. A chant's length sets its output: each line dropped costs a share of output and buys Readiness (casting time), both figures set on the card.
question: What happens when a caster cuts her chant short?

title: Does a technique grow on its own
verbatim: Grows to its Grade. Output rises with the reserve until it reaches the top of the Grade it was designed in; past that it needs an escalated form, with its suffix and a shown cause.
question: As a character climbs Levels, does his technique's output climb with him?

title: Drill and mastery
verbatim: Mastery marks on the card. Three named marks, Held, Drilled and Mastered; each lowers Readiness and cost share by figures set on that card, each crossing a shown cause entered in the chapter-end block.
question: Can drill make a technique itself faster or cheaper?

title: What a vow is worth
verbatim: A great vow, one Grade. As A, and a great vow, one that stakes life, a limb's use or Crystal mass, may lift output one full Grade; nothing lifts it further. A release call stacks on top.
question: How is the output a vow buys measured?

title: What else a vow may be
verbatim: Yes to: A stake beyond Shear Break (A vow may stake life, a limb's use or Crystal mass; broken, the stake is paid at once and for good (R55-1). Under TE5's B, only a staked vow reaches a full Grade); A vow between two (Two people bind each other; each card carries the terms, and whoever breaks them takes the Shear Break).
question: Beyond a permanent narrowing broken by Shear Break, what may a vow be?

title: How a vow is sworn
verbatim: Aloud, any witness. A vow binds when spoken before any living witness, the opponent included; it earns oath experience only at a stone. Somebody always heard, so the counter can be found by asking.
question: What must a vow be to bind: witnessed at a stone, spoken aloud, or held in silence?

title: When a new Trait forms
verbatim: Canon's four, on the page. A new Trait forms only at one of the four events, written as its own scene; no count cap, the scale of the event is the limit.
question: What may form a new Trait in play, and how often?

title: Who writes your character's Trait
verbatim: Natalie writes, you keep. At the event Natalie writes name, Reflection (its kind) and Lattice property; it sticks only when you keep it, as a Third Name does.
question: When a Trait forms in your own character, who writes it?

title: What a Trait entry carries
verbatim: Yes to: Founding sentence (The statement the Continuum accepted, in the bearer's words, yours to write for your characters as in TE11. Denying it is the Shear Break, so every Trait carries a findable counter); Rigidity line (What the bearer cannot safely contradict, as a fact. NPCs play it on the page; for your characters it stays a fact for you to play); Offices held (Which of Bias, Permission, Nucleation and Ceiling it serves; a Permission line lists the signatures it allows).
question: Beside R17-5's Lattice property, which lines does every Trait entry carry?

title: How a Trait evolves
verbatim: The bearer's sentence. The evolved law takes the shape of the sentence the bearer holds in the crisis; for your characters you write that sentence, and the Crystal prints the result.
question: When a Trait fuses or ascends, what decides the shape it takes?

title: New Resonant Pairs
verbatim: New, by R18-2's test. R18-2 extends to Pairs: a new one may be proposed when a build reaches a combination the ten lack, with real mechanism, Grade and effect; it binds once ratified.
question: May new Resonant Pairs be designed beyond canon's ten?

title: Carding a Synergia
verbatim: Drilled, one shared page. One technique page carries both partners, the drill that made it, the cost split and the counter; both cards link to it; no vow.
question: How is a pair's drilled Synergia carded, and what binds the pair?

title: Naming a two-tongue art
verbatim: Each calls his own. The card carries both names, each glossed; in a fight each partner calls it in his own tongue, two calls in one beat.
question: When a Synergia's partners speak different tongues, what is it called?

title: One man's techniques combined
verbatim: A carded composite art. Two of his techniques may be derived into a third, carded art with its own cost, counter and new name; it costs at least the sum of its parts. Chaining stays free.
question: May one practitioner fuse two of his own techniques into a third?

title: What a school keeps back
verbatim: The last form withheld. A school writes its lower forms and teaches its last form mouth to ear; outside the school that form counts as self-derived and is read live.
question: How much of a school's art can an outsider study?

title: Learning by watching
verbatim: Re-derived after watching. A witnessed technique may be re-derived in downtime if the watcher holds its Wellsprings and meets its FOW line; it runs at his stats and becomes his own, with his own name.
question: Can watching a technique teach it?

title: One card shape
verbatim: A table head, then sections. A one-screen head above the seventeen: header, stat line, combat grammar (Verdict, Blade, Percussion or Expenditure), Traits and techniques by name with tell and counter, the voice sample line. Natalie fights from the head.
question: Which shape should every full character card take?

title: The rungs of a person
verbatim: Three rungs. Roster entry; a short card (header, FOW line, Traits by name, one signature technique with tell and counter, voice block, Lore); a full card. Today's compact cards become short cards.
question: How many rungs should a person climb between a walk-on and a full card?

title: What lifts a person a rung
verbatim: Yes to: Stats decide a scene (The first time his stats must decide an outcome on the page, he gets at least a short card before that scene is written); Becomes a rival (A rival under R70-104, spared and returning, gets a full card, since his growth and his debts must be traced); Holds a POV (Anyone whose head a scene sits in gets a full card first, since his readouts come from his own sheet).
question: What should lift a person from the roster to a card, or from a short card to a full one?

title: How much of the sheet
verbatim: Sixty-four on full cards. Full cards carry all sixty-four and the Pool, unset ones spent inside the re-costed totals along the Path and logged, your characters' as CH5 decides; short cards carry Primary totals and the peaks a scene will stress.
question: How much of the stat sheet should a card carry?

title: Who spends a Level's points
verbatim: He builds his own. You spend your characters' points at each Level, build talk welcome; Natalie spends each NPC's where the Level was earned (a Level won by the sword feeds the sword), logged in the changes block.
question: When a Level lands, who spends the points it brings?

title: Four cards past the gate
verbatim: Outliers with Strain. R56-4 extended: each keeps his Level with standing Residual Strain, priced by Part Ten (XP five percent lower, Overchannel and Backlash risk two percent higher, per fifty Levels past). Lorn and Heisuke owe one step now.
question: Four Kharven cast cards stand past a Band gate their Stage has not opened. How are they read?

title: Marking an estimate
verbatim: Tag it inline. One mark, '(est.)', after the figure and nothing more; the six styles collapse into one.
question: How should a card mark a figure canon does not supply?

title: New voice block slots
verbatim: Yes to: Speaker type (The researched real-world model (a customs clerk, a field surgeon, a drover) moves from the notes onto the card, so every return starts from the same voice); Chant tongue (The tongue his chants and release calls run in (his own under R50-26, or a learned one under R70-26, as Kwon's Accord Latin), so Borin's Latin forge-liturgy is caught and fixed); Lying tell (What his body does when he lies or withholds, the body kind of R49-36's three tells, so the frequent lies of R48-42 can be caught by a player who reads bodies).
question: Which slots should join the voice block?

title: Lore and the length cap
verbatim: The seventeen only. The cap binds Identity through Fracture Log; Lore runs free below it. The eight cards over without Lore are trimmed in the sweep.
question: What should the 16,348-character cap bind, now that Lore sections run long?

title: Story fields on the card
verbatim: Yes to: Refusal line (The thing he will not do whatever is offered, as the roster already carries; Table Rule 3's refusals read straight off the card); Conviction (The belief that costs him, named; the Trait System's 'Belief, once survived, becomes law' gets the belief it grows from, and a Shear Break has a truth to break against); Arc kind (Positive, flat, negative or corruption, after K. M. Weiland's arc types: set when the card is made, revised at each arc's end).
question: Which story fields should a full card gain?

title: Skills on the card
verbatim: Skills section, with marks. As A, and each skill carries TE4's three marks (Held, Drilled, Mastered), each crossing a shown cause entered in the chapter-end block. The Crystal never prints them.
question: Where does a skill that is not a working sit on a card, and does drill raise it?

title: A comic name on the card
verbatim: Byname with its making. Byname, who coined it and when, its bank or sound rule, and the given name under it, so a grief beat and the Kharven giving-on have both names to work with.
question: How should a card carry a comic name?

title: A rival between meetings
verbatim: His own clock, shown. A rival's growth runs on a Front (a world clock that ticks between sessions); each tick names its cause, and his return shows it in the room and in what the POV was told.
question: When a recurring NPC, a spared rival above all, comes back, how has he grown since?

title: An old feat too big
verbatim: Keep it, explain it. The feat stays and the card names how (an Overchannel spike, a Domain, a site's Wellspring) and the cost it charged, logged on the Ledger.
question: When converted material claims a feat the new numbers cannot carry, what gives?

title: XP as arithmetic
verbatim: Sums for the carded. Arithmetic for your characters and full cards, the scale for everyone else.
question: Should XP bind as arithmetic, or only set the scale?

title: What training pays
verbatim: Edge, or a sworn drill. A, and a drill sworn as an oath before a Witness Stone pays Part Two's oath XP on swearing and on fulfilment; a broken drill is a strain event. Solo Leveling's contract in FOW's terms.
question: When a downtime turn names training, what does it pay?

title: The record of a climb
verbatim: Yes to: XP bar (XP held and XP to the next Level, from CH14's tally where the card keeps one, so a reader of the card knows how near the next readout is); Level log (Each Level with its cause and the scene it happened in, fed from the chapter-end changes blocks); Stage ledger (Each Stage with its Catalyst, re-assay, witnesses and date, one line of story each, set above the prose Temperance Record, which stays).
question: What should a card record of a character's climb?

title: The next gate
verbatim: Next gate, every card. A line names the next Stage, its FOW Catalyst and any Band gate ahead. NPC cards add the crisis the Fronts are building; your characters' cards name only FOW's Catalyst.
question: Should a card name the gate its bearer faces next?

title: Where the law lands
verbatim: Doc, tools and guides. A, plus the sixth edition of the Ability and Technique Design Guide, the wotr-npc, wotr-stat-line and wotr-write references rewritten, and NATALIE.md's character-sheet line updated, all in this pass.
question: Where should the techniques-and-characters answers land?

title: What joins the card sweep
verbatim: Yes to: One estimate mark (CH7's answer applied to every card, and flags the Level law has since made exact (Borin's, Yoko's reserves) dropped); Lore against body (Each Lore read against its card body; name drift is fixed, and any other contradiction goes to CONFLICTS.md for the docket); Dashes out (Em and en dashes taken out of card bodies and Lore, carrying the prose ban from the page to the sheet).
question: Live law already owes a sweep of names and numbers across all 284 cards; what else should it carry?

title: Which cards first
verbatim: The Kharven room first. Lambert, Bram, Brida, Tabitha Hallenfeld and the rest of the room at Kharven-Seat get their cards first, then the other live threads, then the archive by appearances.
question: Which cards are rebuilt first?

title: Old entries that fail the law
verbatim: Each card an agent ruling. As A, and each card's changed lines go through log_ruling as one agent ruling that quotes them and names its grounds, so you read them in CONTINUE.md and may overturn any.
question: When a carded technique's cost, counter or What nobody knows line fails live law, how is it put right?

title: Proof and the order of work
verbatim: Law and tools, then test. Log the law and rebuild the converter and skeleton; make the three test cards through them; play a scene where one decides a fight; amend; then sweep and rebuilds.
question: In what order does the work run, and what proves it?
